member.name: T:OpenIGI.Composition.TitleCatalog
member.summary: The titles a build can run, shared by every host that runs them.

remarks.para: The only place that names more than one game. Every layering rule about titles exists to keep that true: a host, a renderer or a shared registry that reaches for one by name is a component only that game can use, however well factored everything underneath it is.
Written by hand rather than discovered: a container that found these by reflection would cost the AOT targets their static call graph. A mod edits .

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Composition.TitleCatalog.Titles
member.summary: Gets the titles this build plays, each with everything it brings to the host.
member.remarks: The one list naming both games. A mod adds a title here, or replaces one's package -- its renderers, its scene walk, its player -- keeping its place.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Composition.TitleCatalog.Catalog
member.summary: Gets the catalogue the host resolves titles through.
member.remarks: Every registered package, bound to where the desktop finds it installed. Resolving is free, so it can happen on the frame a player picks a game.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Composition.TitleCatalog.GamePathVariableFor(OpenIGI.Core.Titles.GameTitle)
member.summary: Names the environment variable that says where one title is installed.
member.remarks: Per title, because a machine may well have both games installed and one variable cannot say where two of them are. The names are the ones the test suite already uses, so a shell that can run the retail tests can run the game with no further setting up.

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Composition.TitleCatalog.TryResolve(System.String,OpenIGI.Engine.Titles.IGameTitleRuntime@)
member.summary: Finds the runtime a title id names.
member.param: The id, as -title or the environment gives it; null selects nothing.
Receives the runtime when the id names one.
member.returns: when the id is not a title this build runs.
member.remarks: Case-insensitive, because a command line is typed by a person. An unknown id is reported rather than silently falling back: a run that was asked for one game and quietly gave another is worse than one that stops.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Composition.TitleCatalog.KnownTitleIds

member.name: M:OpenIGI.Composition.TitleCatalog.Probe(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.String},System.String@)
member.summary: Finds a title that is actually installed, when nothing selected one.
member.param: Directories to look in, in order of preference.
Receives where the title was found.
member.returns: The runtime, or null when no title this build runs is installed anywhere it looked.

remarks.para: Each title is tried against its own environment variable first and the shared candidates after, in the order lists them -- so a machine with both installed runs the first, and a machine with only the sequel still starts rather than reporting the first game missing.

A probe rather than a default, because the failure it replaces is a confusing one: pointing the port at an I.G.I. 2 installation and being told there is no config.qvm in it names a file that game does not have.

member.name: P:OpenIGI.Composition.TitleCatalog.SearchPaths
member.summary: Where a title is looked for when its own variable says nothing.
member.remarks: The executable's folder, the app's own, and the working directory — so dropping the port into a game's directory is the whole of the installation procedure. Asked for by process path rather than AppContext.BaseDirectory, because a single-file build unpacks itself into a temporary folder and would otherwise search that.
